items.title: Luis Conte interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 24, 2025
items.q: The label is Willie Colon and Eddie Palmieri. ... I bought an Eddie Palmieri “Azucar Pa Ti.” I still have them.

ctx.x: I bet you had some revelations along the way. I mean at that time there was some hit records by those fellas. Like “Watermelon Man” and some of the more accessible tunes.

Yeah, yeah. And I started hearing all this stuff from other friends that knew about this, “Oh right, you’ve got to listen – Mongo,” you know, so-and-so, that I had met. I met -- another guy that was going to LACC also, his name was John Montealegre was his last name. He was an African-American man but with the last name Montealegre and he lives in Pasadena, and he had a set of congas. So we hit it off, and I would go and hang out with him with a couple of friends, you know young guys you know just partying Friday…

had I bought a Willie Colon record, I bought a Puente album, and I bought an Eddie Palmieri “Azucar Pa Ti.” I still have them. And it’s just – it was all happening man. But it just, you know for me to go into, if you play a little funk I’ll just figure something out. And I’ve heard the tambourines and I’ve heard all that before. I’ll say one thing I would know – sometimes if you listen to some songs – I can’t think of them now – sometimes the conga pattern was turned around as a Cuban would play it. You know and…
